purpose: Compact, source-linked CS1 base-game planning rules consumed by deterministic tools. Rules produce hints and pacing limits only; they never authorize a mutation or bypass a gate. Full notes: docs/research/cs1-planning-knowledge-zh-TW.md.

growthPacing.rationale: Growables only spawn on vacant zoned cells while demand is positive and residential tax is the main early income, so vacant supply should lead high demand. A per-wake cap keeps zoning in small repeated batches, which avoids the same-age cohorts that cause death waves. Live evidence: with 24-cell targets every new block was absorbed within one ~25-game-day wake while demand stayed at or above 50, so targets were doubled and the cap raised to 4 blocks. Live evidence (~4,500 residents): demand settled at 40-49 in every category while developable vacancy fell to 14/3/1 cells, so growth stalled with positive demand; a 24-cell tier from demand 30 keeps one block of supply ahead of moderate demand. Live evidence (~9,300 residents): with demand 53-60 the 48-cell tier allowed one block per wake, every block was absorbed within that wake (developable vacancy stayed at 26 cells) and population grew ~20 per wake; a 96-cell tier zoned three blocks per wake and growth rose to ~53 per wake with unchanged happiness and traffic.

utilityBudget.rationale: Below 100% a budget B gives service level (B/10)^2 percent; lower an oversupplied utility and raise it again as demand grows.

milestones.rationale: Population thresholds vary by map and internal milestone names are not display names, so the next milestone is the first one whose unlock capability is still locked. Early milestones pay a cash bonus and unlock services, so early population growth is the main economic lever.

zoning.industryResidentialBuffer: about two city blocks, preferably with trees or offices between

roads.arterialAdvice: few connections, avoid four-way junctions and traffic lights
